title: Coefficient cocycle of the normalized pro-etale derived direct-image comparison
statement:
For finite commutative rings $A,B,C$ and homomorphisms $\varphi:A\to B$, $\psi:B\to C$, put $\chi=\psi\varphi$. For each scheme $T$ use constant ring sheaves on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $r_{\varphi,T}$ for restriction of module-sheaf scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and for its exact termwise functor on the unbounded derived categories. Write $\rho_T:r_{\varphi,T}r_{\psi,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}r_{\chi,T}$ for the canonical identification: on underlying abelian sheaves it is the identity and the two actions are $a m=\psi_T(\varphi_T(a))m$; on derived categories it is its termwise localization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

Let $p:Z\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes. Let $P_R=Rp_*^R:D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},R)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ be the K-injective-defined direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For $\theta=\varphi,\psi,\chi$, let $\beta_\theta:P_R r_{\theta,Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}r_{\theta,Y}P_S$ be the specified natural isomorphism of [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars], for the corresponding ring map $\theta:R\to S$. Thus for a K-injective complex $H$ over $S_Z$ and a K-injective resolution $a:r_{\theta,Z}H\to I$ over $R_Z$, its component, using the canonical derived evaluation identifications, is $[p_*a]^{-1}$. Here brackets denote localization, and a K-injective complex receives only null-homotopic maps from acyclic complexes.

This normalization uniquely determines $\beta_\theta$ among natural isomorphisms with these endpoints. For every $L\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},C)$ one has
$$\beta_{\chi,L}\circ P_A(\rho_{Z,L})=\rho_{Y,P_CL}\circ r_{\varphi,Y}(\beta_{\psi,L})\circ\beta_{\varphi,r_{\psi,Z}L}.$$
No coefficient restriction is assumed to preserve K-injective complexes, and no properness, boundedness, flatness or constructibility assumption is imposed.

proof.text: For a K-injective B-complex H choose a K-injective resolution j of its scalar restriction, using the existing HasKInjectiveResolutions instance for module-valued sheaves. The supplied normalization theorem [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars] and the normalization hypothesis for gamma have the same right side. The image of j under direct image is a quasi-isomorphism by the supplied theorem, so its localization is invertible. Cancel this map and the two canonical evaluation isomorphisms to identify the components at Q(H).

For arbitrary L choose an isomorphism e:L -> Q(H) with H K-injective, using DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isKInjective and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Naturality transports the equality of components at Q(H) to L; cancel the functorial image of e. Extensionality gives equality of natural isomorphisms.

Prove the coefficient-pasting calculation by private helpers in the item module, retaining the argument previously read in the quarantined Sheaf.Paper.FiniteCoefficientDirectImage without importing that unavailable module. The supplied underived mate identity [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars] gives the scalar/pullback unit identity. Transpose along the ordinary pullback/direct-image adjunction to prove the two-coefficient chain with the sectionwise identity associators. Pass this identity through exact localization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], using mapDerivedCategorySquareIso_hom_app_comp, and transport along the canonical leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory isomorphisms. A generic mate-pasting calculation follows by transposing along the last adjunction, its counit identity and naturality. Apply it to the C-, B-, and A-coefficient derived adjunctions. The actual definition in [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars] identifies these mates with the inverses of the specified beta comparisons. Thus beta_chi inverse is rho_Y inverse followed by r_phi,Y(beta_psi inverse), beta_phi inverse at r_psi,X(L), and P_A(rho_X). All calculations use arbitrary schemes and commutative rings.

Package the four factors from the preceding equality as an isomorphism z. Equality of their hom maps gives beta_chi inverse = z. Apply congrArg Iso.inv, obtaining beta_chi = P_A(rho_X inverse), followed by beta_phi, r_phi,Y(beta_psi), and rho_Y. Precompose with P_A(rho_X), use functoriality and the isomorphism cancellation law, and obtain the asserted cocycle. No coefficient restriction is assumed to preserve K-injective complexes.
